capitals.name: Saint-Quentin
capitals.note: Inferred: the Vermandois page names Saint-Quentin only as Eleanor's title in 1191 ('Countess of St Quentin'); no page opened names the seat before that.

keyframe_review.note: 17,405 km2 (bbox 1.4-4.2 E, 49.05-50.4 N). The Vermandois page has no infobox and no area, and names no extent in 990-1076; unverified, kept as drawn (page budget). Herbert IV is count 1045-1080 (his page).

19,332 km2: the 990 outline plus a 2,500 km2 piece at 3.0-3.7 E, 48.9-49.3 N, which fits the county of Valois (no gazetteer region). 'Count Herbert IV received the county of Valois through his wife' in 1077 and, after his death in 1080, his son-in-law Hugh Magnus inherited 'the countships of Vermandois and Valois' (Herbert IV page): Cliopatria's 1085 is a few years after the pages. Kept.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape unchanged but holding only to 1166: 'After Ralph II's abdication, Elisabeth and Philip inherited the County of Vermandois' in 1167 and it was held jointly with Flanders until 1191

keyframe_review.note: 19,332 km2, the same outline since 1085. Years only: Cliopatria draws the county to 1168 and then gives it to its Flanders shape (36.8k km2 = 17.6k Flanders + 19.3k Vermandois in 1169-1187), a year after the page's 1167.

correction.text: from 1191, when 'Eleanor (d. 1213) had a life interest in eastern Vermandois with the title Countess of St Quentin' and 'The king took possession of Péronne and its dependencies immediately'

keyframe_review.note: 19,510 km2 for 1188-1209. The Vermandois page has Philip of Alsace keep Vermandois 'until his death in 1191' (the 10 March 1186 treaty only ceded it to the king and left him the title for life, Philip I page), so the county is Eleanor's only from 1191 and without Péronne; the 40 km radius round Péronne is the researcher's reading of 'Péronne and its dependencies'. Eleanor kept Valois under the 1182 treaty (her page) and it stays in the outline.

correction.text: the same county to 1213 only: 'Upon Eleanor's death, King Philip took over control of all of Eleanor's property'

keyframe_review.note: 19,510 km2 for 1210-1215. Eleanor died on 19 or 21 June 1213 (lead of her page; the body says 1213/1214), when the county passes to the crown; Cliopatria keeps it two more years.

region.text: the county of the Vermandois, Cliopatria's 990 outline

ledger.note: 990: the County of Vermandois, with Saint-Quentin and Péronne, enters the record. Page silent on the county's origin; 990 is Cliopatria's first year for the row.

1077: Herbert IV takes Valois. 'Count Herbert IV received the county of Valois through his wife'; after Herbert's death in 1080 'his son-in-law inherited the countships of Vermandois and Valois' (Herbert IV page). The region is Cliopatria's 1085 addition (2,500 km2 at 3.0-3.7 E, 48.9-49.3 N), read as Valois; Cliopatria dates it to 1085.

region.text: the County of Vermandois, inherited by Elisabeth and Philip of Flanders

ledger.note: 1167: Vermandois passes to Flanders. 'After Ralph II's abdication, Elisabeth and Philip inherited the County of Vermandois'; Elisabeth, Raoul I's elder daughter, had married Philip of Alsace, count of Flanders, in 1156. The Vermandois page has them hold Vermandois, Valois and Amiens 'conjointly' from 1167 to 1183. Cliopatria draws the land inside its Flanders shape from 1169.

1183: after Elisabeth's death Philip II 'moved to seize the province of Vermandois on behalf of Elisabeth's sister, Eleonore'; Eleanor's page has Philip of Flanders refuse her the county and her appeal to the king. The page dates no fighting; Philip II's victory at Boves is undated there.
1186: peace between Philip II and Philip of Flanders. On 10 March 1186 Philip accepted 'the cession of Vermandois to the king' but kept the title Count of Vermandois for life.

region.text: eastern Vermandois, Eleanor's life interest as Countess of St Quentin

ledger.note: 1191: Philip of Alsace dies at Acre on 1 August and Vermandois falls to Eleanor and the crown. 'A treaty with Philip Augustus let the Count of Flanders keep Vermandois until his death in 1191'; then 'Eleanor (d. 1213) had a life interest in eastern Vermandois with the title Countess of St Quentin. The king took possession of Péronne and its dependencies immediately.' Eleanor's page puts Philip's death in 1192 (the Philip I page and this one give 1191).

region.text: the County of Vermandois, annexed to the royal domain

ledger.note: 1213: Eleanor dies without children (19 or 21 June) and the county passes to Philip II. 'Upon Eleanor's death, King Philip took over control of all of Eleanor's property'; Philip II was to annex Vermandois to the royal domain if she died without children (condition of 1192/1191).

wars.name: War over the Vermandois succession
wars.outcome: Philip II backed Eleanor against her brother-in-law Philip of Alsace after Elisabeth's death; the peace of 10 March 1186 ceded Vermandois to the king while Philip kept the title for life, and he held the land until his death in 1191.
wars.note: Eleanor's page dates the Treaty of La-Grange-Saint-Arnoul to 20 March 1182 (Eleanor keeps Valois) and mentions Philip II's victory at Boves without a date; the Boves page would not load. Both are before Elisabeth's death (1183) on that page, an order the page itself finds inconsistent.

certainty.note: A feudal county drawn from Cliopatria's outline; the cession of Péronne and the 'eastern Vermandois' of 1191 have no boundary on any page opened.

notes:
Gaps in Cliopatria explained by the ledger: 1169-1187 (Vermandois inside the Flanders shape, 1167 inheritance by Elisabeth and Philip of Alsace; the Flanders dossier should gain the county in 1167 and give it up in 1191, not 1188); the 1188-1190 years of Cliopatria's second shape fall while Philip still holds the county (title for life, 'until his death in 1191'). Cliopatria ends the county in 1215, two years after Eleanor's death (1213).
Disagreements between pages: Valois came to Herbert IV in 1077 'through his wife' (Vermandois page) but the Herbert IV page does not date it; Eleanor's page has Philip of Flanders die in 1192 and an arrangement then (Philip I page and Vermandois page: 1 August 1191); Eleanor's page keeps Valois with her from 20 March 1182 while the Vermandois page has Elisabeth and Philip hold Valois and Amiens jointly until 1183. The Treaty of Boves page would not load (url_not_found), so the 1185 stage of the war is undated. Amiens is named on the Vermandois page as held by Elisabeth and Philip from 1167 but is not separated in the ledger.
Not modelled: the later history on the Vermandois page (1435 Treaty of Arras, Valois-Burgundy; 1477 repossession by the crown), outside Cliopatria's rows. Counterpart without a dossier: County of Valois (1077; Valois lands at 49.1-49.4 N, 2.9-3.7 E). Gazetteer names needed: Péronne (place), Valois (region). Vassalage: Cliopatria lists the county as a member of (Kingdom of France) throughout; the pages opened do not discuss homage.
Page budget: four pages opened (limit five).
